title: Bronze Serpent and Victories

questions.question: Which Canaanite king fought against Israel and took prisoners?
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:1 (ESV): "The king of Arad... heard that Israel was coming... and he fought... took some of them captive."

questions.question: What vow did Israel make to God regarding the Canaanites?
options: "If you will give this people into my hand, I will devote their cities to destruction."
questions.correctAnswer: "If you will give this people into my hand, I will devote their cities to destruction."
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:2 (ESV): "And Israel vowed a vow to the Lord and said, 'If you will indeed give this people into my hand...'"

questions.question: Why did the people become impatient on the way around Edom?
options: The journey was long and hard, and they lacked food and water
questions.correctAnswer: The journey was long and hard, and they lacked food and water
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:4-5 (ESV): "And the people became impatient on the way... 'Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness?'"

questions.question: What did God send among the people as punishment for complaining?
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:6 (ESV): "Then the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people..."

questions.question: What did Moses make to save the people?
options: A bronze serpent set on a pole
questions.correctAnswer: A bronze serpent set on a pole
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:9 (ESV): "So Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on a pole."

questions.question: What happened if a bitten person looked at the bronze serpent?
options: He was healed of all diseases
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:9 (ESV): "And if a serpent bit anyone, he would look at the bronze serpent and live."

questions.question: Israel defeated Sihon king of what people?
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:21, 23 (ESV): "Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites... Sihon gathered all his people... and fought..."

questions.question: Israel defeated Og king of what place?
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:33 (ESV): "Then they turned and went up by the way to Bashan. And Og the king of Bashan came out..."

questions.question: What was the name of the place where they defeated Arad?
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:3 (ESV): "So the name of the place was called Hormah (Destruction)."

questions.question: Where did Israel camp after defeating Og?
options: In the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: In the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:1 (often grouped with end of 21 narrative): "Then the people of Israel set out and camped in the plains of Moab..."

questions.question: What song did Israel sing at the well calling "Spring up, O well!"?
options: "Spring up, O well! - Sing to it!"
questions.correctAnswer: "Spring up, O well! - Sing to it!"
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:17 (ESV): "Then Israel sang this song: 'Spring up, O well!—Sing to it!'"

questions.question: Heshbon was the city of which king?
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:26 (ESV): "For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites..."

questions.question: What river marked the border between Moab and the Amorites?
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:13 (ESV): "For the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites."

questions.question: The "Book of the Wars of the Lord" is mentioned in connection with what?
options: Waheb in Suphah and the valleys of the Arnon
questions.correctAnswer: Waheb in Suphah and the valleys of the Arnon
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:14 (ESV): "Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord, 'Waheb in Suphah...'"

questions.question: Did God tell Moses to fear Og?
options: "Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand"
questions.correctAnswer: "Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand"
questions.explanation: Numbers 21:34 (ESV): "But the Lord said to Moses, 'Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand...'"

key_verse_text: So Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on a pole. And if a serpent bit anyone, he would look at the bronze serpent and live.
